# package cotp

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-cotp"
```

Package cotp implements a TP0 (Class 0) COTP transport service over RFC 1006 TPKT, plus a full X.224 TPDU codec.

Service API (preferred for applications):

	Connect / Accept → *Conn → ReadTSDU / WriteTSDU / Close

Connect and Accept take ownership of the net.Conn immediately, perform the Class 0 CR/CC handshake using go-tpkt internally, and return an open \*Conn. Consumers of \*Conn must not use go-tpkt. A \*Conn is full duplex: a reader and writers run concurrently, concurrent writers are serialized per TSDU, and each operation's context bounds only its own direction (SetReadDeadline or SetWriteDeadline). Close unblocks outstanding operations. A context that ends an operation before any octet moved leaves the connection open; once octets have moved, it aborts the connection.

Codec API (tools / low-level): Decode / MarshalBinary on individual TPDU payloads (no TPKT header). See docs/COMPLIANCE.md and docs/TP0\_API\_DESIGN.md.

Do not pass an entire TPKT packet to Decode.

API philosophy:

  - Strict on malformed structure: reject invalid wire data; no silent normalization.
  - Explicit over magical: behavior is documented; no hidden defaults beyond documented canonical marshal.
  - Preserve wire information where possible: unknown parameters and structural variants are kept for replay and debugging.
  - No hidden normalization beyond documented canonical marshal behavior.
  - Correctness first, convenience second: safe for protocol tooling and production use.

Codec policies (documented intentional behavior):

  - LI must cover the TPDU fixed part (X.224 13.2.2.1); undersized LI returns ErrInvalidLI.
  - CR/CC user data after the header is exposed and round-tripped; CR total length ≤ 128 octets.
  - Duplicate known CR/CC parameters (0xC1/0xC2/0xC0/0xF0) follow X.224 13.2.3: last value wins.
  - Canonical CR/CC encode order (0xC1, 0xC2, 0xC0, 0xF0) is a local deterministic choice, not an X.224 mandate.
  - Preferred maximum (0xF0) is typed as wire units; generic codec has no ITOT 511-unit clamp.
  - LooksLike\* helpers are classification-only and use the same type masks as PeekType/Decode.
  - A DT is the class 0 and 1 format (LI 2) or the normal class 2 to 4 format (an even LI of 4 or more). An odd LI is the extended format (X.224 13.7.4 NOTE) and is rejected with ErrUnsupportedDTVariant.
  - DC, ER, AK, EA and RJ carry no user data: octets after their header are ignored on decode and not kept.
  - Encoders check the lengths they write and otherwise write what they are given: CDT is written as its low 4 bits and TPDU-NR as its low 7 bits, and (\*DT).MarshalBinary does not refuse a DT that DecodeDT would reject (see its comment).

Slice aliasing: Returned \[]byte fields (e.g. Parameter.Value, selector slices) may alias the input buffer. Callers must copy if they need to retain or mutate data beyond the lifetime of the input slice. This aliasing behavior is part of the package contract and must not change silently across minor releases. A returned field has no capacity beyond its own octets, so an append to it allocates and never writes into the input buffer or into another field.

Replay/debug: DecodeWithRaw(b) returns Decoded with Raw set to the exact input slice b (may alias). Decode does not set Raw. On decode error, no partial value is returned, so Raw is unavailable.

Multi-octet fixed fields (e.g. refs) are decoded and encoded in network byte order (big-endian).

## Functions

### func ExtractUserData

```go
func ExtractUserData(b []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

ExtractUserData returns the user data payload of a DT or ED TPDU from b. The buffer must be a complete COTP TPDU; PeekType must be TypeDT or TypeED. For passive decoding or handoff, use Decode then branch on Type; DT.UserData and ED.UserData are the payloads for the next protocol (e.g. S7comm, MMS). The returned slice may alias b; callers must copy if retaining beyond the lifetime of b.

### func HeaderLength

```go
func HeaderLength(b []byte) (int, error)
```

HeaderLength returns the total header length in octets: 1 (LI) + LI value. So the header occupies b\[0 : 1+LI]. Returns an error if b is too short or LI is invalid.

### func PreferredMaxTPDULength

```go
func PreferredMaxTPDULength(units uint32) (uint64, error)
```

PreferredMaxTPDULength returns the effective TPDU length in octets for the given preferred-maximum wire units (units × 128).

This is a generic X.224 codec helper: units == 0 is rejected; there is no RFC 1006/2126 (ITOT) 511-unit ceiling here.

### func PreferredMaxTPDUUnits

```go
func PreferredMaxTPDUUnits(length uint64) (uint32, error)
```

PreferredMaxTPDUUnits returns the exact preferred-maximum wire units for an effective octet length. The length must be a positive multiple of 128 and fit in a uint32 unit count. No flooring is performed.

### func ReadLI

```go
func ReadLI(b []byte) (uint8, error)
```

ReadLI returns the length indicator from the first octet of b. LI is the header length in octets excluding the LI octet itself and user data (X.224). Valid range is 0–254. Returns ErrTooShort if len(b) \< 1, ErrInvalidLI if LI > 254.

CR is a Connection Request TPDU (X.224 13.3). Nil selector = absent; non-nil empty slice = present with length 0. TPDUSize / PreferredMaxTPDUSize nil = parameter absent. type Conn struct {

Conn is an established Class 0 (TP0) COTP connection over a stream.

A Conn comes from Connect or Accept. The zero value is not a connection: its ReadTSDU and WriteTSDU return ErrClosed at once, and its Close returns ErrClosed.

#### func Accept

```go
func Accept(ctx context.Context, conn net.Conn, cfg ServerConfig) (*Conn, error)
```

Accept performs the responding TP0/ITOT handshake on conn.

Ownership of conn transfers immediately. On any error, conn is closed and must not be used further. On success, the returned Conn owns the stream.

#### func Connect

```go
func Connect(ctx context.Context, conn net.Conn, cfg ClientConfig) (*Conn, error)
```

Connect performs the initiating TP0/ITOT handshake on conn.

Ownership of conn transfers immediately. On any error, conn is closed and must not be used further. On success, the returned Conn owns the stream.

#### func (Conn) Close

```go
func (c *Conn) Close() error
```

Close performs the TP0 T-DISCONNECT operation by closing the underlying stream.

Close is safe to call more than once and from multiple goroutines, and concurrently with ReadTSDU and WriteTSDU: a blocked operation returns ErrClosed, and so does every later one. The stream is closed and the local reference released exactly once, before the first Close returns.

Close does not return nil. It returns ErrClosed when it ended the connection, and on every later call; when the connection had already ended for another reason (the peer went away, a protocol error, a context that ended an operation after octets had moved), it returns that first cause. Nil-receiver Close is not promised.


LocalAddr returns the local network address, or nil.

#### func (Conn) ReadTSDU

```go
func (c *Conn) ReadTSDU(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error)
```

ReadTSDU receives one complete TSDU by reassembling minimal Class 0 DT segments until EOT=1. The returned slice is the caller's: it has no capacity beyond its length, go-cotp keeps no reference to it, and a later call never changes it.

One reader at a time reassembles a TSDU; a concurrent caller waits its turn and returns ctx.Err() if ctx ends first. ctx bounds only the read direction (SetReadDeadline); a concurrent WriteTSDU is unaffected. If ctx ends the read before any octet of the TSDU arrived, ReadTSDU returns ctx.Err() and the connection stays open; once octets have been consumed, the connection is aborted.

Memory: the segments received so far are held in one buffer, whatever their size and number. Its capacity never exceeds MaxTSDULength; while it grows, and when the result is handed over, the old and the new buffer exist together, so a call holds less than twice MaxTSDULength, plus the TPKT packet being read (at most 65535 octets). A partly received TSDU is held until the call returns: until the final segment arrives, ctx ends, the stream fails or the connection is closed. A read loop without a deadline keeps it for as long as the peer leaves the TSDU unfinished.

#### func (Conn) RemoteAddr

```go
func (c *Conn) RemoteAddr() net.Addr
```

RemoteAddr returns the remote network address, or nil.

#### func (Conn) WriteTSDU

```go
func (c *Conn) WriteTSDU(ctx context.Context, tsdu []byte) error
```

WriteTSDU sends one complete TSDU as one or more minimal Class 0 DT segments. Empty or locally oversized TSDUs are rejected before protocol I/O.

Concurrent writers are serialized for the entire segmented transfer, so segments of different TSDUs never interleave; a writer waiting its turn returns ctx.Err() if ctx ends first. ctx bounds only the write direction (SetWriteDeadline); a concurrent ReadTSDU is unaffected. If ctx ends the write before any octet of the TSDU reached the stream, WriteTSDU returns ctx.Err() and the connection stays open; once octets have moved, the stream may hold a partial TSDU and the connection is aborted.

### type DT

```go
type DT struct {
	EOT            bool
	TPDUNR         *uint8
	DestinationRef *uint16
	Parameters     []Parameter
	UserData       []byte
}
```

DT is a Data TPDU (X.224 13.7). v1 supports minimal (class 0/1) and normal (class 2–4) formats. Nil UserData or zero-length = valid empty payload. Nil DestinationRef/TPDUNR = absent (e.g. minimal format). UserData may alias decode input; see package doc.

#### func DecodeDT

```go
func DecodeDT(b []byte) (*DT, error)
```

DecodeDT decodes a Data TPDU from b. v1 supports the class 0 and 1 format (LI=2) and the normal class 2 to 4 format (an even LI of 4 or more).

The extended class 2 to 4 format has a 7-octet fixed part, so its LI is odd: X.224 §13.7.4 NOTE states the rule that an even LI is the normal format and an odd LI the extended one. DecodeDT follows it: an odd LI of 5 or more is rejected with ErrUnsupportedDTVariant, as are LI 0, 1 and 3.

Returned UserData and Parameter values alias b and have no capacity beyond their own octets; see package doc.

#### func (DT) MarshalBinary

```go
func (d *DT) MarshalBinary() ([]byte, error)
```

MarshalBinary encodes the DT as a COTP TPDU (X.224 13.7). Minimal format (no DestinationRef, no variable part): LI=2, 2-octet fixed part. Normal format: LI=4+len(variable), 4-octet fixed part, then variable, then user data. UserData nil or zero-length is valid (empty payload). Deterministic for same DT.

MarshalBinary writes what it is given. TPDUNR is written as its low 7 bits. Parameters are written in both formats, although X.224 13.7.1 a) gives the class 0 and 1 format no variable part, and a variable part of odd length makes LI odd. DecodeDT rejects an odd LI (ErrUnsupportedDTVariant) and reads every LI of 4 or more as the normal format, so it does not return such a DT as it was built.

Decoded is the result of Decode or DecodeWithRaw. Exactly one of CR, CC, DT, DR, DC, ER, ED, AK, EA, RJ is non-nil; Type matches it. Zero value is not a valid decoded result.

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) (Decoded, error)
```

Decode parses a complete COTP TPDU from b and returns a Decoded struct. On success, exactly one of CR, CC, DT, DR, DC, ER, ED, AK, EA, RJ is non-nil and Type matches it. On error, the returned Decoded is the zero value; it is never partially filled.

```go
func DecodeWithRaw(b []byte) (Decoded, error)
```

DecodeWithRaw is like Decode but on success sets Decoded.Raw to the exact input slice b. Raw may alias b; callers must copy if retaining or mutating beyond the lifetime of b. On error, returns zero Decoded (Raw is unavailable by design).

### type NegotiatedParameters

```go
type NegotiatedParameters struct {
	Class           Class
	MaxTPDULength   int
	LocalRef        uint16
	RemoteRef       uint16
	LocalSelector   []byte
	RemoteSelector  []byte
	PeerConnectData []byte
}
```

NegotiatedParameters are frozen after a successful CR/CC handshake. All slices are defensive copies. Selector nil means absent; non-nil empty means present len 0. On the client RemoteSelector is the CC's responding selector when the CC carries one (it may differ from ClientConfig.RemoteSelector), otherwise the requested one; on the server LocalSelector is the responding selector sent in the CC and RemoteSelector the CR's calling selector.

### type ServerConfig

```go
type ServerConfig struct {
	// LocalSelector default accept policy:
	//   nil            → no called-selector requirement
	//   non-nil empty  → CR must present CalledSelector of length 0
	//   non-empty      → CR must present CalledSelector equal exactly
	LocalSelector []byte
	MaxTPDULength int
	MaxTSDULength int
	// OnConnect decides accept/reject. Nil = defaultAutoAccept.
	// Indication fields are defensive copies (safe to retain).
	//
	// OnConnect runs on the goroutine that called Accept, after the CR was
	// read and before the CC is written, with the context given to Accept
	// and while that context's deadline is armed on the stream. No Conn
	// exists yet, so it has nothing to call back into. A callback that
	// blocks stalls that handshake only; no other connection waits for it.
	// It is not interrupted when the context ends: the CC write that follows
	// then fails. A panic in OnConnect is not recovered: it reaches the
	// caller of Accept, after Accept has closed the stream.
	OnConnect   func(context.Context, ConnectIndication) (AcceptDecision, error)
	SizeProfile SizeProfile
	// EchoSelectors returns the CR's transport selectors in the CC
	// (X.224 §13.3.4: "If a Transport-Selector is given in the request it
	// may be returned in the confirmation"): the calling selector as 0xC1
	// and, as the responding selector 0xC2, LocalSelector when non-nil,
	// otherwise the CR's called selector. A selector absent from the CR
	// stays absent. False (the default) sends only LocalSelector, as before.
	EchoSelectors bool
}
```

ServerConfig configures the responding TP0/ITOT handshake (Accept).

### type SizeProfile

```go
type SizeProfile int
```

SizeProfile selects local CR/CC size-parameter encoding and how omitted peer selections are interpreted for the TP0/ITOT service layer.

```go
const (
	// SizeProfileRFC1006Compat: installed-base CR/CC omission rules;
	// accept legacy and preferred CRs; respond based on what the peer proposed.
	SizeProfileRFC1006Compat SizeProfile = iota
	// SizeProfilePreferredMaximum: always propose 0xF0 (with 0xC0 fallback);
	// require explicit selected-size on incoming CC; still decode legacy CR.
	SizeProfilePreferredMaximum
)
```

### type TPDUType

```go
type TPDUType uint8
```

TPDUType is the X.224 TPDU type code (high bits of octet 2). Low bits carry CDT/options for some types (e.g. CR, CC, DT).

```go
const (
	TypeCR TPDUType = 0xE0 // Connection Request (1110 xxxx)
	TypeCC TPDUType = 0xD0 // Connection Confirm (1101 xxxx)
	TypeDR TPDUType = 0x80 // Disconnect Request (1000 0000)
	TypeDC TPDUType = 0xC0 // Disconnect Confirm (1100 0000)
	TypeDT TPDUType = 0xF0 // Data (1111 000y)
	TypeER TPDUType = 0x70 // TPDU Error (0111 0000)
	TypeED TPDUType = 0x10 // Expedited Data (0001 0000)
	TypeAK TPDUType = 0x60 // Acknowledge (0110 zzzz)
	TypeEA TPDUType = 0x20 // Expedited Acknowledge (0010 0000)
	TypeRJ TPDUType = 0x50 // Reject (0101 zzzz)
)
```

#### func PeekType

```go
func PeekType(b []byte) (TPDUType, error)
```

PeekType classifies the TPDU from the first two octets (LI and type code). It performs only minimal LI sanity; full header/variable-part validation is done by per-TPDU decoders. Returns TypeED, TypeAK, TypeEA, TypeRJ for those codes; reserved/invalid codes return ErrInvalidTPDUCode or ErrReservedTPDU.

#### func (TPDUType) String

```go
func (t TPDUType) String() string
```

String returns the TPDU type name for debugging and logging.
